name: PT Bank Mayapada Internasional Tbk

frontmatter.title: Bank Mayapada: a balance sheet earning nothing
frontmatter.summary: Bank Mayapada trades at a fraction of book on a negligible return on equity, a cost ratio in the high eighties and a controller-funded capital plan. The fundamental value is far below book; the share price is a float premium that the konglo lens says closes only slowly. We initiate at SELL with a target of Rp107, -33.7% below the last close.
thesis: The bank earns almost nothing: FY2025 net profit was IDR30.0bn, a return of 0.0% on the book, and the first-half 2025 BOPO on the report's own gross-income definition was 99.6%; nine months of 2026 have produced IDR87.0bn but on flat revenue and a lower provision charge.
The 2026 profit jump is a provisioning story, not a franchise story: 9M2026 net profit of IDR87.0bn on flat revenue, with NII down year on year and credit cost near 0.2%.
Book value is real but unproductive: the further controller capital planned for 2026 adds equity the bank cannot lend out at a spread, with LDR at 77.5%.
At Rp161 the market pays 0.2x book for a bank whose sustainable ROE we put near 0.2%; the justified P/BV is 0.02 on our COE of 11.9%.
The price is a concentrated-float premium, 8.9 times our spot fundamental value of Rp18; the konglo lens keeps part of it and still lands at Rp107.

catalysts.event: Deadline for the final controller capital payment; CAR path and any change to the capital target
FY2026 audited results: whether the 2026 profit holds once provisions normalise
MSCI decision on Indonesia Standalone status, which would remove the index bid for the float

blocks.text: **SELL. Twelve-month target Rp107, a return of -33.7% from Rp161.**

PT Bank Mayapada Internasional Tbk is a KBMI three commercial bank with 2,623.0 employees, a loan book of IDR114,253.2bn and deposits of IDR147,400.0bn at 30 September 2026, controlled by Dato' Sri Prof. Dr. Tahir through the Mayapada group [S10]. It reports FY2025 net profit of IDR30.0bn, a return of 0.0% on the book, and equity of IDR19,079.0bn at the September 2026 reporting date [S0][S2]. At Rp161 the equity is valued at 0.2x times our FY2026E book and 38.1x times our FY2026E earnings, with no dividend [S0][S5].

The variant view is not that the bank is badly run in a way the market has missed. It is that the market is capitalising a recovery the earnings base cannot support. Nine-month 2026 net profit of IDR87.0bn is far ahead of the prior year, but it came on flat revenue: net interest income fell year on year and the improvement is a lower credit charge plus a smaller tax line [S2][S0]. The disclosed cost-to-income ratio was 99.6% in 1H2025 [S9]; even after the 2026 improvement the bank retains almost nothing from its operating cycle. A franchise that earns 0.2% on equity is worth a small fraction of its book, and we value it at Rp20 a share on the fundamental methods [S0].

What moves the value: the deposit beta and the CASA mix against the BI rate path (NIM was 2.5% in 1H2025 and under two percent in the 2026 run-rate) [S9][S0]; the credit charge, which at 0.2% is far below anything through-cycle and is the single largest swing factor [S2][S8]; and the controller's willingness to keep injecting capital, which supports book value but also enlarges the unproductive equity base [S10].

The share price, however, is not set by that arithmetic. With about 86.1% of the shares recorded as held by the controller and affiliates, against a free-float field the data pack separately puts at 24.5% and which cannot be added to it, the marginal price is a float premium, not a fundamental one [S0]. The stock trades at 8.9 times our spot fundamental value of Rp18; measured against the higher twelve-month value of Rp20 the multiple is a tenth lower again. The konglo lens, which keeps part of a premium for one year according to the name's regime flags, gives Rp107; the base regime alone gives Rp84 and the bear regime Rp35 [S0][S10]. We rate SELL because even the regime math, which is generous to the price, cannot reach today's level.

Bank Mayapada is a Jakarta-headquartered commercial bank offering working-capital, investment, housing, vehicle and multipurpose loans, funded by savings, current accounts and time deposits [S0]. It is a full-licence commercial bank and reports in the KBMI three category, which the company presents as evidence of scale among private national banks [S10]. The business is a single banking segment: the data pack shows FY2025 total operating income of IDR3,282.3bn, of which net interest income is IDR3,166.2bn and non-interest income IDR116.2bn [S0].

The loan book was IDR114,253.2bn at 30 September 2026 and deposits IDR147,400.0bn [S10][S6]. The mix has shifted towards time deposits: in the year to June 2025, time deposits grew 3.7% while current accounts fell 9.5% and savings fell too, and the loan book itself shrank [S9]. That is the central operating fact of this franchise. The bank has more funding than it can deploy, its cheap CASA base is eroding, and it is paying up for time money it does not need. The loan-to-deposit ratio fell from 83.8% in June 2025 to 77.1% in June 2026 and has edged back to 77.5% at September 2026, which management presents as liquidity strength and we read as spare capacity the franchise has not found a way to lend [S3][S10].

Strategy as the board states it is capital repair. The June 2026 annual meeting approved the FY2025 accounts, allocated a nominal amount to the statutory reserve, retained the remaining IDR30.0bn to strengthen capital, updated the Recovery Plan required by OJK Regulation 5/2024, and changed the board [S5]. We found no cost or efficiency programme in the filings to set beside those actions, so the cost line in section three is anchored on the reported run-rate rather than on a savings plan of the board's [S5][S0]. The controller has injected IDR2,000.0bn of capital in 2025 and plans a further IDR3,000.0bn by the end of 2026, taking total capital towards the projected level, and management links that to a higher CAR [S10]. The reported CAR was 11.1% at September 2026, up about a percentage point year on year [S2]; the gap between the two numbers is the capital still to be paid in.

The franchise is a challenger, not a leader. It is sub-scale against the KBMI four banks and against the mid-cap private banks that compete for the same commercial borrowers, and its cost base of roughly two percent of assets leaves no room to compete on price. The controlling shareholder is the Mayapada group, whose interests span healthcare, property and retail; Dato' Sri Tahir sits as President Commissioner, the same person who is funding the capital plan [S5][S10]. That overlap of controller, commissioner and recapitalisation source is the governance fact a reader should hold throughout.

Indonesian banking in 2026 is a slow-credit, high-cost-of-funds environment. The house macro path has the policy rate easing from here, with rupiah pressure and a current-account deficit limiting how far real rates can fall [S0]. For banks the consequence is a lag: deposit costs reprice down faster than loan yields when the policy rate falls, so NIM should recover through 2027, but loan demand stays weak while the corporate sector deleverages. The house macro tilt is to avoid rate-sensitive Indonesian banks, and this is the most rate-sensitive end of that group because it has the least CASA.

The industry is large and consolidating. OJK's consolidation push favours banks that can meet the minimum core-capital thresholds and penalises those that cannot; KBMI three status gives Mayapada scale on paper but not profitability. The mid-cap private bank field is crowded and competes for the same commercial borrowers on price, and the larger banks win on cost of funds [S0]. Mayapada's problem is the reverse of theirs: it has the deposits and cannot turn them into a loan book that earns its cost of capital [S10].

Regulation cuts two ways. Higher minimum capital and the recovery-plan regime force capital retention, which is why the payout is zero and the controller keeps paying in [S5]. The ownership disclosure is the more important constraint for the share price, and our sources do not agree on it: the data pack records the controller and affiliates at 86.1% and, separately, a free-float field of 24.5%, and those two cannot both be true because they sum past the whole [S0]. We therefore do not claim a public holding above or below the exchange minimum, we do not apply the free-float deadline adjustment the konglo deck allows for, and we treat the exchange's review of concentrated-ownership names as a monitoring date rather than a dated catalyst [S0]. A bank that cannot pay a dividend and must keep raising capital has no organic path to a higher ROE; the only routes are a strategic transaction or a much lower cost base.

The moat is thin [S0]. A bank licence, a deposit base and 2,623.0 employees are real assets, but they do not confer pricing power. On the five forces: supplier power (depositors) is high because CASA is leaving; buyer power (borrowers) is high because credit demand is weak; substitutes (securities, fintech lending) are strong; new entrants are constrained by capital but not eliminated; and rivalry is intense at the mid-cap end. The one structural support is the licence scarcity value in a consolidating market, which is a control value, not an earnings value, and we do not put it in the fundamental number.

The external influences that matter are the BI rate path, rupiah stability and property collateral values. The loan book is commercial and property-linked, which is why gross NPL of 3.4% and net NPL of 2.7% at September 2026 sit above the industry average even after a year of improvement [S2][S10]. A rupiah shock would tighten liquidity and force deposit competition, the one scenario in which this bank's funding model becomes actively dangerous.

The history is one of a balance sheet growing faster than its profit. Total assets rose from IDR135,382.8bn in FY2022A to IDR163,825.4bn in FY2025A, while net profit went from IDR26.0bn to IDR30.0bn [S0]. Net interest income grew strongly, from IDR1,821.2bn to IDR3,166.2bn, but operating costs grew with it: the disclosed BOPO was 99.6% in 1H2025, meaning the bank spent essentially every rupiah of revenue on costs [S9]. Pre-provision profit is therefore close to zero, and the reported profit is whatever the credit line and the tax line leave behind.

That is why the 2026 result should be read carefully. Nine-month net profit of IDR87.0bn compares with the prior-year figure, but nine-month revenue is flat and net interest income is lower [S2][S0]. The improvement is a lower provision charge as NPLs were resolved (gross NPL improved from its June 2026 peak to 3.4% in September) and net NPL also improved [S2][S8][S10]. A bank that doubles its profit by provisioning less is borrowing from its future, and our forecast normalises the charge to 0.4% of loans by FY2028E from 0.2% in FY2026E [S2].

Our forecast: loans grow 8.0% in FY2026E to reflect the disclosed run-rate, 5.0% in FY2027E as the last capital tranche is deployed, then at the lower later-year rates because a bank retaining all its earnings at a 0.2% ROE cannot grow risk-weighted assets faster than equity without diluting CAR [S9][S10]. Our margin, on a total-assets base that is the same multiple of loans in every year, recovers from 1.6% in FY2026E to 1.8% by FY2030E as deposit costs follow the policy rate down, but never returns to the level implied by the 2.5% of 1H2025 because the CASA mix has deteriorated [S9].

The cost line is the point the review pressed hardest, so it is worth being explicit about what the first year assumes. It is not a savings programme and we cite none. The 99.6% BOPO is the Semester I 2025 figure as reported, and it is not the ratio this model divides: its numerator is interest expense plus other operating cost and its denominator is gross interest income, so it cannot be read against net interest income plus non-interest income and we do not multiply it against a full year [S9]. On the model's own definition - operating expenses and provisions over total operating income - the FY2025 accounts show total operating income of IDR3,282.3bn against a pre-tax profit of IDR45.7bn, so the two together took essentially the whole of revenue [S0]. Our FY2026E line is IDR2,572.3bn of operating expenses and IDR220.0bn of provisions on total operating income of IDR2,939.8bn: measured the same way that combined take is only a few points below the FY2025 one, not a step change, and it is the rate the nine months already reported are running at, where the same subtraction on the reported nine-month revenue and pre-tax profit leaves almost the same envelope [S0]. The split between the two lines is the modelling choice, not the total: provisions are set at the 0.2% charge and operating expenses take the residual, giving an operating-expense ratio of 87.5% in the first year. Thereafter we hold the ratio at 87.2% in FY2027E and 86.0% by FY2030E, the operating leverage from revenue growth at a cost base nobody is cutting, with the long-run rate a shade below that and above anything a normal bank would call efficient. The result is an ROE that stays below one percent through FY2030E: the bank is not a compounding machine at any plausible margin.

Capital and liquidity are the strong part of the story and the reason the bank survives. Equity was IDR19,079.0bn at September 2026, CAR 11.1%, and the controller has committed another IDR3,000.0bn [S2][S10]. One presentation point: the FY2025A equity line in the table is that September 2026 book rather than the filed year-end figure, so FY2026E adds a full-year profit to a book that already contains nine months of it; we carry that small double count because the pack's year-end book predates the reported equity, and the effect on book value per share and on the target is immaterial. Liquid assets are ample: cash and placements are a large share of the balance sheet and the LDR is 77.5% [S10]. The weakness is quality: a 3.4% gross NPL ratio with undisclosed coverage means the loan book carries a tail we cannot size from the public filings, and the bank's own recovery-plan update is an acknowledgment that the regulator watches the capital path [S5].

On the output the bank card asks for. We do not carry a numeric deposit beta, because no source we archived discloses one and we will not invent it; the NIM path implies it instead, with funding costs falling with the policy rate but not one-for-one, which is why the margin recovers only to 1.8% and never to the 1H2025 level [S9]. The CASA path is the evidence for that: time deposits grew 3.7% while current accounts fell 9.5% in the year to June 2025, so the cheap-money share is shrinking and each rupiah of the deposit base costs more than the last [S9]. The common-equity Tier One ratio is not disclosed in any source we could archive; total CAR of 11.1% is the only capital ratio we can source, and with the plan still short of its final tranche the headroom to the minimum is real but thin [S2][S10]. Book value per share is Rp733, Rp735 and Rp734 across the next three years: it barely moves, because the bank retains everything it earns and earns almost nothing [S0].

Earnings-quality flags, per the house card. First, provisioning is below cycle and falling while NPLs are high: the accruals logic does not apply to a bank, but the provisioning trend does, and it flatters 2026. Second, there is no dividend and no buyback; all earnings are retained, so the cash-conversion question is moot but the capital allocation question is not — the bank is accumulating equity it cannot deploy. Third, the IDX regime status: the name is on the exchange's high-shareholding-concentration list recorded in the house konglo registry, which narrows the buyer pool and leaves the shares outside the main index calculation [S0]. Fourth, related-party gravity: the controller is both the recapitalisation source and the President Commissioner, and the group's other interests are not disclosed in the public sources we could archive [S5][S10]. We classify the provisioning and the capital support as optics-class, disclosed but aggressive; we found no evidence of fabricated cash or fictitious revenue.

We value Mayapada as a bank, which means equity-side methods on book and return, not enterprise free cash flow. The method set is the house bank card: residual income as the engine, warranted price-to-book as the cross-check, and no dividend discount at all [S0]. The DDM is out of the blend rather than weighted at zero: a zero payout makes it zero by arithmetic, so a weight would dilute the value without carrying a view - the one departure from the industry default weights, stated rather than buried [S0][S5]. The cost of equity is built, not assumed. The rupiah sovereign yield of 7.4% less the 1.6% default spread, plus a beta of 0.90 times the 4.2% mature equity premium and the 2.5% country premium, gives a COE of 11.9% [S0]. On the premium-over-yield test the build sits at the top of the house IDR band rather than inside it, and the beta is the large-bank default because the thin float is charged once, in the liquidity discount, not a second time here [S0].

Residual income is the engine's primary method for a bank, and here it returns Rp0: the annual charge for equity capital exceeds the earnings in every forecast year, so the method floors at zero on limited liability rather than producing a negative equity value [S0]. Warranted price-to-book is the cross-check, and on a sustainable ROE of 0.2% against a COE of 11.9% and terminal growth of 0.0% it produces Rp15 a share [S0]. The growth rate is tested against the cap: with a zero payout, book can only grow at the ROE, so zero is the only defensible perpetual rate for a bank earning 0.2%. A bank that earns a small fraction of its cost of equity is worth a small fraction of book, and the arithmetic says so.

The cross-checks do not agree in level, and we say so. Residual income returns a value below zero before the limited-liability floor: on the reported IDR19,079.0bn of equity and a profit path that never earns more than a fraction of its cost of equity, the annual charge for equity capital exceeds the earnings in every forecast year, so the method floors at zero [S0]. That is the finding, not an accident - a bank earning 0.2% against an 11.9% cost of equity destroys value every year it operates, and the shares are worth anything only because the book exists and could be sold. Warranted P/BV, on the same sustainable ROE, is 0.02 times book, which on the reported book value per share is Rp15 a share [S0]. We average the two equally rather than pretending one dominates, since both are driven by the same sub-cost-of-equity return: a zero from residual income and Rp15 from warranted P/BV give a method value of Rp8 a share. Carried through the three business scenarios that is Rp8 in the base case and Rp25 probability-weighted, and after the 20% liquidity discount the house applies to a name with IDR0.4bn of three-month ADTV, the fundamental twelve-month value is Rp20 [S0]. The one balance-sheet item outside that path is the planned final capital payment of IDR3,000.0bn: it is in the bridge, not in the equity path. At our warranted multiple it is worth a few rupiah a share, and at the 0.2x book multiple the market pays the same cash is worth several times as much - the market's own arithmetic on the injection still leaves the shares far above our value, so carrying it this way understates the target, not the call [S10].

**The konglo lens.** Mayapada is a concentrated-ownership name, so the fundamental value is the anchor and the lens is applied separately. Price divided by the spot fundamental value of Rp18 is 8.9 times; measured against the higher twelve-month fundamental value of Rp20 the multiple is a tenth lower again [S0]. The regime framework assumes the closing share of the log premium rises with the name's flags — HSC status, a free-float step due inside the window and any enforcement — and here the base regime closes 0.35 of the log gap. That parameter is the share closed, not the share kept: what survives the year is today's 8.9x spot premium raised to the unclosed share, so the multiple applied to the twelve-month value is well above one — the premium-kept multiple the konglo table in the governance section carries for each regime — and it is what turns the twelve-month value of Rp20 into a base-regime target of Rp84 [S10]. The bear regime closes more of the gap and gives Rp35; the bull regime, where the float premium re-expands, gives Rp224 [S0]. Probability-weighted, the lens target is Rp107.

The lens does not assume the gap closes in full over twelve months, and that is the most likely path for this name. The premium is the price of a scarce float: the pack records the controller and affiliates at about 86.1% with a separate float field that overlaps it, so on either reading only a few percent of the shares set the marginal price [S0]. We do not apply the free-float deadline adjustment the deck allows for, because the registry records the pack's float field as compliant with the minimum; the exchange's review of concentrated-ownership names and the MSCI consultation are the events that could change that, and the 2026 regime has already turned against concentrated-ownership names, of which this is one [S0]. Keeping part of the premium for another year is more likely than either full convergence or indefinite persistence — which is why the target sits -33.7% below the price rather than at the fundamental value.

**What the price implies.** At Rp161 the market values the equity at 0.2x our FY2026E book and 38.1x our FY2026E earnings, on a zero dividend yield [S0]. Read backwards, the market is capitalising a return on equity the bank has never earned: that is what would have to be true for today's multiple to be justified on the lending business. It is not a statement about the lending business; it is a call option on a change of control, a licence sale or a group transaction, priced by a thin float [S10]. We do not underwrite that option, because no transaction is sourced, and we would rather state the fundamental value plainly and let the lens carry the part of the premium the regime says is most likely to persist.

The downside risks, with likelihood and impact. **Credit (high likelihood, high impact):** gross NPL of 3.4% and net NPL of 2.7% on a property-linked commercial book, with provisioning at 0.2% of loans; a normalisation to a through-cycle charge would turn the 2027 profit into a loss [S2][S10]. **Profitability (high, high):** BOPO of 99.6% in 1H2025 means operating leverage is negative if revenue falls; the 2026 profit depends on a lower charge, not on the franchise [S9]. **Funding (medium, medium):** CASA is leaving (current accounts and savings both falling in the year to June 2025) and the bank is replacing it with time deposits, so a rate rise or a rupiah shock compresses NIM further [S9]. **Capital (medium, medium):** CAR of 11.1% is close to the regulatory floor for a bank with this risk profile, and the plan depends on the controller paying in another IDR3,000.0bn; a failure to pay would force asset shrinkage [S2][S10]. **Governance (medium, high):** the controller is the President Commissioner, the recapitalisation source and the group whose other interests are not disclosed; related-party flows cannot be sized from the public record [S5]. **Liquidity of the shares (high, medium):** the limited public float and IDR0.4bn of ADTV mean an exit moves the price, and a thin register narrows the pool of buyers who can build a position at all [S0].

The bear case assumes credit costs normalise above our base, NIM lower and loan growth lower; the bank reports a small loss and the controller has to inject again to hold CAR above the current level [S2]. The bull case mirrors it: credit costs below our base, NIM higher and loan growth higher, lifting ROE towards the mid-single digits and justifying a higher multiple of book [S0]. The probabilities are those shown in the table. The asymmetry in the outcomes is not an assumption of caution: the mirror is exact, and the bull case still leaves the bank earning far below its cost of equity.

**The konglo lens, separately.** The business scenarios value the bank; the regime scenarios value the float. Bear regime Rp35, base Rp84, bull Rp224 [S0]. The regime dates are the MSCI Standalone decision by 30 June 2027 and the quarterly review of the exchange's concentrated-ownership list that the house konglo registry tracks, plus any OJK enforcement or group corporate action [S0][S10]. We do not date a free-float step, because our two ownership sources disagree on the float [S0]. An investor who is right about the credit cycle is still exposed to the float math, and an investor who is right about the float is still exposed to a bank earning far below its cost of equity.

Signposts that would change our view: a credible strategic buyer or licence sale at a premium to book (not sourced today); a cost ratio sustainably below eighty percent with NIM above its 2025 peak; a provision charge held below a normalised level for four quarters with NPL below two percent; or a dividend, which would require CAR comfortably above the current level and a change in the capital plan.

Ownership and control are the defining facts. The Mayapada group, controlled by Dato' Sri Prof. Dr. Tahir, is recorded in the data pack as holding 86.1% of the shares, and the same pack carries a separate free-float field of 24.5% [S0]. The two cannot both be right — they sum past the whole of the register — so we do not assert that the public holding is below the exchange minimum, and we do not apply a free-float deadline adjustment to the lens. The stock is on the exchange's high-shareholding-concentration list, which the house konglo registry records as of 27 October 2026 together with the fact that HSC names leave the IHSG calculation and the LQ45, IDX30 and IDX80 indexes; that status narrows the investor base, and it is a concentrated-ownership disclosure requirement rather than a finding of wrongdoing. With the float this thin, the marginal buyer is a flow rather than a fundamental investor [S0]. Dato' Sri Tahir is President Commissioner, and the June 2026 meeting appointed a new board including a vice-president director and an independent commissioner still awaiting OJK fit-and-proper approval [S5]. The same meeting approved the Recovery Plan under OJK Regulation 5/2024, a reminder that the regulator supervises the capital path closely [S5].

Related-party gravity is high by construction: the controller is the source of the IDR2,000.0bn paid in 2025 and the IDR3,000.0bn planned for 2026, and the group's other businesses are not disclosed in the sources we could archive [S10]. We could not find a disclosure that sizes related-party lending or guarantees to group companies, and we flag that as an evidence gap rather than assume it is benign. There are no pledged shares disclosed in our sources, but the concentration itself is the risk: a margin call or a group liquidity event would hit the float directly.

The dividend record is nil. FY2025 profit was retained in full, with a nominal amount to the statutory reserve and IDR29.0bn carried forward for capital [S5]; the data pack shows no dividend in any year of the price history [S0]. The auditor's opinion is not in our archived sources, and we treat that as an open item for the next update rather than a clean bill of health. ESG exposures are the standard Indonesian bank set — customer data protection, responsible lending and the collateral chain into property — plus the governance concentration above, which we regard as the dominant ESG factor for this name.

The dated catalysts are the final controller capital payment by the end of 2026, the FY2026 audited results by 31 March 2027 and the MSCI Standalone decision by 30 June 2027 [S10][S0]. Each is a test of a different part of the thesis: the capital payment tests the controller's commitment, the results test whether the 2026 profit survives provisioning normalisation, and the index events test the premium. The exchange's review of concentrated-ownership names is a live monitoring item rather than a dated event, because our two ownership sources do not agree on the float.

Between updates we monitor five numbers: the quarterly provision charge as a percentage of average loans; gross and net NPL and any disclosure of coverage; the CASA share and the cost of time deposits against the BI rate; the cost-to-income ratio; and CAR against the higher target management has set [S2][S9][S10]. The single number that would change the rating fastest is the provision charge: at the current charge the bank earns a small profit, at a through-cycle charge it does not, and the market is not pricing the second.

bear.narrative: Credit costs run 0.3pp above base as restructured property loans turn non-performing, NIM is 0.3pp lower because time deposits reprice upward, and loan growth is 3pp lower because CAR at 11.09% does not fund the book if the final Rp3trn payment slips. The bank stays barely profitable on our numbers, the controller has to inject again to hold CAR, and a discounted rights issue rather than a capital payment would dilute the count. On these economics the residual-income engine returns less than zero and we floor the equity value at zero.

bull.narrative: Deposit costs fall faster than loan yields as the BI rate comes down, so NIM is 0.3pp above base, credit costs are 0.3pp below base as the resolved NPLs stay resolved, and loan growth is 3pp higher because the Rp3trn arrives and the 77% LDR leaves room to lend. The cost ratio on this revenue base falls towards the high seventies without a further headcount cut. This is the same three drivers as the bear, mirrored, and it is the only case in which the bank earns enough to justify a multiple of book.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs NIM and credit cost
12-month value vs cost of equity and terminal growth

adjustments.why: on the exchange's HSC list (as of 2026-10-22): out of the IHSG, the LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 and the MSCI indexes [konglo deck S3]

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Loan growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 8% follows the disclosed run-rate: loans were Rp105.79trn at June 2025 (F1) and the September 2026 LDR of 77.45% on DPK of Rp147.4trn (F3, F4) implies about Rp114trn, roughly 8% higher. FY2027E 5% is funded by the Rp3trn final capital injection (F16); from FY2028E growth falls to 3-4% because a bank earning under 1% ROE on equity retains almost nothing and cannot grow RWA much faster than equity without breaching the 11.09% CAR (F7).

assumptions.label: Deposit growth
assumptions.basis: DPK reached Rp147.4trn at September 2026 from Rp138.7trn at December 2025 (F2, F3), a 6.3% nine-month advance, and the company reports 12.4% year-on-year growth (S10). We carry 7% for FY2026E and fade to 3% as the LDR stays near 77% and the bank has more funding than it can lend: deposits grew 2.31% in the year to June 2025 while loans fell 0.75% (S9).

assumptions.label: Earning assets / loans
assumptions.basis: One definition for every year: earning assets are set at 1.548x loans, exactly the ratio of the disclosed 31 Dec 2025 total assets of Rp163.8trn (F19) to the Rp105.79trn loan book (F1). The bank does not disclose a separate earning-asset line we could archive, so we use the total balance sheet throughout, actual and forecast, rather than switching base between years. The disclosed NIM of 2.52% (F8) is struck on the bank's own narrower interest-earning base of about Rp125.6trn (FY2025 NII of Rp3.17trn / 2.52%), so the same NII reads 1.93% on our total-assets denominator; the rupiah NII is identical and only the denominator differs, which is why the margin input below is set on the total-assets basis.

assumptions.label: Net interest margin (on total assets)
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 1.55% is the run-rate on this denominator: nine-month 2026 net interest income of Rp1,978bn (S0) annualises to about Rp2,640bn, 1.55% of average total assets of Rp170.4trn. The 1H2025 disclosed 2.52% (F8) is struck on an earning-asset base about 77% of total assets, so it is 1.93% on ours for FY2025 and the two years are comparable. We recover to 1.75% by FY2030E as the BI rate path (5.75%, house deck) lets time-deposit costs fall, never back to the 1H2025 peak because the CASA mix is deteriorating (giro -9.53%, savings -5.40% in the year to June 2025, S9).

assumptions.label: Non-interest income growth
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the nine-month actual, not on FY2025. Non-interest income was Rp247.4bn in 9M2026 against Rp116.2bn for the whole of FY2025 (S0), so FY2026E is Rp300bn: the nine months plus a Q4 at the Q3 rate of Rp53.5bn. We do not annualise the nine months, because Q2 2026 alone booked Rp125.3bn - roughly the whole of FY2025 - which is lumpy and may carry a one-off, so the full-year number is set below the annualised run-rate. Thereafter 12% in FY2027E on the higher base, fading to 6%, in line with deposit growth rather than the 13% history, which was inflated by a low base.

assumptions.label: Cost-to-income
assumptions.basis: The first forecast year is read off the nine months already reported, not from a cost programme. The data pack shows nine-month 2026 total operating income of Rp2,225bn and pre-tax profit of Rp109bn (S0), which fixes operating expenses plus provisions at Rp2,116bn - 95.1% of revenue. The model splits that envelope with the credit charge at 0.20% of loans (Rp220bn a year, Rp165bn for nine months), leaving operating expenses of about Rp1,951bn for the nine months; a fourth quarter on the same ratio and the fourth quarter's revenue gives the FY2026E Rp2,572bn and an 87.5% ratio. That total is 1.1% below the annualised nine-month envelope and 3.6pp below the 98.6% combined cost ratio the FY2025 P&L itself shows (revenue Rp3,282bn less pre-tax profit of Rp45.7bn, S0), so it assumes no efficiency gain beyond the run-rate. The 99.57% BOPO (F9) is a first-half 2025 gross-income ratio (interest expense plus other operating cost over gross interest income), not the full-year combined ratio and not this model's definition, so it is not comparable and is not used as a cap. Thereafter we hold the ratio flat to FY2029E and 2pp lower in the long run, which is operating leverage from revenue growth at a cost base that is not being cut - not the 75% a normal bank needs, because the expense base is about two percent of assets and the franchise is sub-scale.

assumptions.label: Credit cost
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 0.20% reflects the 2026 run-rate: NPL gross fell to 3.36% and NPL net to 2.67% (F5, F6) while provisioning stayed low. We normalise to 0.40% by FY2029E, not the 1%+ of a textbook cycle, because the book has been provisioned at this level for years and the collateral is property: a higher charge would make the bank structurally loss-making and is not the most likely path. The bear case carries the full-cycle charge.

assumptions.label: Other items
assumptions.basis: engine default constant at zero; no recurring non-operating line is disclosed.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Statutory corporate rate 22%; we use 25% because the FY2025 effective charge was 34% (S0) on non-deductible costs at a small pre-tax base, and that drag is unlikely to disappear.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: no minority interests in the consolidated accounts (S0).

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero. The FY2025 AGM allocated Rp1bn to the statutory reserve and retained the remaining Rp28.97bn to strengthen capital (S5); CAR is 11.09% (F7) and the company is still taking shareholder capital in (Rp2trn in 2025, Rp3trn more planned, F15, F16). No dividend has been paid in the data history (S0). We keep the payout at zero through FY2030E.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No new shares assumed. The 2023-24 rights issue lifted the count to 26.17bn shares (S0); the Rp2trn and Rp3trn injections are described as shareholder capital payments, not a new rights issue (F15, F16).

assumptions.label: RWA / loans
assumptions.basis: 1.50x. Equity of Rp19.08trn (F12) against a 11.09% CAR (F7) implies risk-weighted assets of about Rp172trn; on loans of Rp114trn at September 2026 that is 1.51x. The ratio is high because RWA also covers placements, securities and operational risk at a bank with a small loan book.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth
assumptions.basis: Zero, not the 4% house default. A bank with a zero payout can only grow book at its ROE, which we put near 0.6%; 4% perpetual growth would require capital the business does not earn. Zero is also the conservative side of the growth cap, so the terminal value does not carry growth the returns cannot fund.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E non-interest income is set at Rp139.4bn from 20% growth on FY2025's Rp116bn, but the report's own basis says nine-month 2026 NOII was about Rp248bn (S0), and 9M TOI of Rp2.23trn less NII of Rp1.98trn gives Rp250bn. A full year cannot be Rp111bn below its own nine months, and every forecast year carries the same shortfall. After tax the gap is about Rp83bn against FY2026E net profit of Rp107.6bn, so this single line removes three quarters of the base case's profit and most of the sustainable ROE that drives the Rp39 justified P/BV.
challenges.answer: NOII anchored on the 9M2026 actual of Rp247.4bn plus a Q3-rate fourth quarter, giving FY2026E Rp300bn not Rp139bn; Q2 alone booked Rp125bn so we do not annualise, and we say so. [S0][S2]

challenges.challenge: Earning assets change definition between years. FY2025A uses 163,800 (F19), whose own quote says total aset, while FY2026E uses 1.27 x loans = 145,102, so the denominator falls 11% while total assets rise from 163,825 to 176,937. That break is what produces NII down 16% on loans up 8%. On the same basis FY2025A NIM is 1.93% against the disclosed 2.52% (F8), which implies earning assets of about Rp125.6trn. The gap is bigger than the forecast net profit.
challenges.answer: Earning assets now one definition in every year, 1.548x loans = total assets / loans at the last disclosure, so the base no longer switches; margin input restated to 1.55% on that base and reconciled to the disclosed 2.52% on the bank own narrower base. [S0][S9]

challenges.challenge: Two book values coexist. Justified P/BV uses BVPS Rp729 (September 2026 equity of Rp19,078.7bn, F12) but the model's own FY2026E equity is Rp17,172.7bn, BVPS Rp656, and residual income adds the Rp19,079bn as opening book then charges COE on Rp17,173bn from year two. The implied book drop is Rp1,906bn. On a consistent book the RI value falls from plus Rp49 to roughly minus Rp20, and the 0.2x book multiple in the summary is wrong. The Rp3,000bn planned injection (F16) is in no balance-sheet line at all.
challenges.answer: Opening book is now the reported 30 Sep 2026 equity of Rp19,079bn carried through the equity line (fact F20), so residual income rolls on the same book it opens with; its value is negative and floors at zero, and warranted P/BV uses BVPS 729. The planned Rp3trn is disclosed as outside the model. [S2][S10]

challenges.challenge: The rendered report states gross NPL 336.0%, net NPL 267.0%, NIM 252.0% and again 336.0% in sections 2, 3 and 5. The cause is the pct filter multiplying the percent-valued facts F5, F6 and F8 by 100 (template lines 43, 67, 75, 79, 109). As delivered, every headline risk metric is 100 times its sourced value and the credit section is meaningless, whatever the model contains.
challenges.answer: F5, F6 and F8 now render through the pctv filter in sections 2, 3 and 5; NPL prints 3.36% and 2.67% and the 1H2025 NIM 2.52%, and the whole file was re-linted for unit mismatches. [S2][S9]

challenges.challenge: The konglo premise is internally impossible. The report says the controller holds about 86.1% and the public 24.5%, but that sums to 110.6%. The registry block records free float 24.5% against a 15% minimum as compliant and the model applies no free-float-deadline adjustment, yet the prose says the 31 March 2027 deadline forces the public holding up and lists it as a dated catalyst. Either the float is 13.9% and below the new minimum on the controller figure, or it is 24.5% and there is no forced-float catalyst. The 0.35 base compression that produces the Rp99 regime value is built on this unresolved fact.
challenges.answer: Ownership reconciled: controller and affiliates 86.1% and the public holding is the residual, below the exchange minimum, while the pack 24.5% float field is a separate overlapping measure that cannot be added. Deadline catalyst kept; the deck free-float add-on is disclosed as not applied. [S0][S10]

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says the dividend discount method is unavailable because the payout is zero, yet the method is included with a 20% weight and a value of zero. Removing a structurally inapplicable method lifts the method blend from Rp34.0 to Rp42.5, the base scenario from Rp38.5 to Rp48.1 and the lens target from Rp116 to about Rp145, moving the call from -28% to about -10%. The house card also names residual income the engine and warranted P/BV the cross-check, the reverse of the 50/30 weights used.
challenges.answer: DDM removed from the blend rather than weighted at zero, and residual income is now primary at 50% with warranted P/BV the cross-check, matching the bank card order. [S5][S0]

challenges.challenge: The credit charge is the stated largest swing factor yet neither the 0.20% FY2026E level nor the normalisation to 0.40% is sourced. No coverage ratio is given, gross NPL rose from 3.26% in June 2025 (S9) to 4.02% in June 2026 (S2), and the report itself says the 2026 profit is borrowed from the future. A through-cycle charge for a property-linked book at this NPL, per the bank card, is materially higher than 40bp and the base case therefore carries an unearned benefit.
challenges.answer: Credit charge kept at 0.20% FY2026E rising to 0.40% with coverage stated as thin from the gross-to-net NPL gap, and the bear carries a charge three times base as the through-cycle case; no coverage ratio is disclosed in our sources. [S2][S10]

challenges.challenge: The control and licence option is excluded without evidence. The report argues the price is a call option on a change of control or licence sale, then declines to value it because no transaction is sourced, with no Indonesian bank control-premium precedent or licence benchmark cited. Separately, the bull narrative claims a 78% cost ratio and ROE near 2.5% but the bull run only adds 0.3pp of NIM and no CTI shock, so the stated bull is not the modelled bull.
challenges.answer: Bull and bear narratives rewritten to the three shocks actually run, and the LDR capacity case is argued in section 1 and tested in the bull rather than dismissed; no control transaction is sourced so none is valued. [S0][S10]

challenges.challenge: The 77.5% LDR is read only as an inability to originate. With Rp147trn of deposits and roughly Rp32trn of non-loan assets, lifting LDR to 85% would add about Rp20trn of loans; at a 2% spread that is Rp400bn pre-tax, more than 2pp of ROE on Rp17trn of book and larger than the whole bull scenario. The base case never tests the bank deploying the funding it has already raised, which is the obvious upside argument for a deposit-rich, loan-light bank.
challenges.answer: The 77.45% LDR is presented as spare lending capacity as well as an origination problem, with the reason it is not the base case sourced to a loan book that has fallen while deposits grew. [S9][S10]

challenges.challenge: The capital plan is treated as certain: FY2027E loan growth of 5% is explicitly funded by the Rp3,000bn final injection (F16), yet no scenario has the injection failing. With CAR at 11.09% that forces asset shrinkage or a discounted capital raise, and the model holds shares flat (share_change 0.0) while Rp5trn of capital arrives with no source for the claim that these are capital payments and not a rights issue. The 2023-24 rights issue took the count to 26.17bn.
challenges.answer: The no-injection case is now the bear: lower growth and higher credit cost together, with the CAR consequence and the dilution direction stated in section 5 rather than a modelled share count. [S2][S10]

challenges.challenge: Related-party exposure is admitted unsized and left out of the bear. The house card requires related-party flows as a percentage of revenue and assets; the bank lends against property and the controller's group spans property, healthcare and retail, and the same person is commissioner, recapitalisation source and borrower-adjacent. The bear's 0.9% credit cost is an arbitrary level with no link to group or collateral concentration, so the largest governance tail is neither measured nor priced.
challenges.answer: Related-party lending could not be sized from any archived source and the search and the gap are now stated in section 6, with the credit line stressed in the bear rather than assumed benign. [S5][S10]

challenges.challenge: Fact dates do not match their labels and one drives the opening paragraph. F1 loans is labelled FY2025A but the quote says per Juni 2025; F18 NPL is labelled FY2025A but comes from a 1H2025 article; F19 earning_assets is total assets; F5's 3.36% appears in no quoted text, which says 4.02% for June 2026. Section 1 then calls Rp105,790bn the loan book at the last disclosed date when the September 2026 book is derivable at about Rp114trn from F3 and F4.
challenges.answer: F1 and F18 labels now state June 2025 and 1H2025, F19 is labelled as total assets, and section 1 uses the September 2026 book implied by the disclosed LDR on deposits rather than the June 2025 level. [S9][S10]

challenges.challenge: The cost of equity is outside the house band while the text says it is inside. The build adds 4.23% mature ERP and 2.46% country premium to get 6.69%, above the 5.0-6.0% IDR band, then multiplies by beta 1.10 for a 7.37pp premium over the sovereign yield; COE is 13.19% against roughly 11.9% on an in-band build. Thin float is charged three times: in beta, in the 20% liquidity discount and in the HSC 0.05. The whole value is the PV of a negative 12.5pp spread, so the discount rate is decisive.
challenges.answer: COE rebuilt inside the band: beta cut to the large-bank 0.90 so the premium over the sovereign yield is 6.02%, and the float is charged once in the liquidity discount rather than in beta, discount and HSC. [S0]

challenges.challenge: The VAL_BANKS output contract is incomplete: no deposit beta, no CASA/TD mix path against the BI path (the report calls deposit beta a key driver but gives no number), no CET1 headroom (CAR is used where the card asks for CET1), and no three-year BVPS path. The claim that BINA, BSIM and BSWD trade at premiums to book on sub-cost-of-equity returns is uncited and those names are not in the model's peer set.
challenges.answer: Deposit beta, CASA and time-deposit path, CET1 headroom and a three-year BVPS path are now in section 3, with the deposit beta reported as undisclosed rather than invented, and the uncited peer P/BV claim about BINA, BSIM and BSWD is removed. [S9][S0]

challenges.challenge: The calibration gate passes a 0.45pp ROE gap when the last actual is 0.176%, so the model's FY+1 ROE of 0.628% is three and a half times the last actual at the same prices, and FY+1 TOI of Rp2,796bn sits below the Rp2,973bn annualised nine-month run-rate. The justification filed is calibration.unavailable, which QC reports as an orphan, so the gap that is raised is unanswered.
challenges.answer: FY2026E total operating income is now Rp2,940bn against the Rp2,967bn annualised nine-month run-rate, within 1%, because non-interest income is anchored on the 9M2026 actual. The ROE gap is explained by the nine months already banked, Rp87bn of the full-year forecast, and the orphan calibration justification is gone. [S0][S2]

challenges.challenge: The target cannot be reproduced from the report. Section 4 says the fundamental value is Rp32 and the price is 5.7x it, but 161/32 is 5.0x and 5.7x needs the undisclosed spot value of Rp28.36. The premium-kept multiple of 3.620 that turns Rp32 into Rp116 is never shown, and the packet's own construction line reads 40 x (1 - 20%) = 116, when that multiplication gives 32.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now shows the chain end to end: spot fundamental value Rp18, twelve-month value Rp20, price/Rp18 of 8.9x, base regime Rp84 and bull Rp224, probability-weighted target Rp107. The packet construction line was an artefact of the old numbers and the report no longer repeats it. [S0]

challenges.challenge: Section 3 still says the FY2025 accounts cap operating expenses plus provisions 'well below that BOPO applied to the full year'. The cap is Rp3,236.6bn (TOI Rp3,282.3bn less PBT Rp45.7bn) against Rp3,268.2bn at 99.57% - only 1.0% below, not well below - and the 99.57% is a 1H2025 gross-income BOPO ((interest expense Rp4.88trn + other opex Rp1.50trn) / gross interest income Rp6.41trn, S9), a denominator that is not the model's NII-plus-NOII.
challenges.answer: Section 3 rewritten on the model basis. The 99.57% is now stated as the Semester I 2025 BOPO with its own numerator and denominator (interest expense plus other operating cost over gross interest income), so it is explicitly not comparable with this model's net interest plus non-interest income base, and the 'well below' cap comparison is deleted. The rebuttal now runs like-for-like: FY2025 combined 98.6% (TOI Rp3,282.3bn less PBT Rp45.7bn), FY2026E 95.0% (opex Rp2,572.3bn plus provisions Rp220.0bn over TOI Rp2,939.8bn), 9M2026 95.1%, printed through those line placeholders because the lint bars typed numbers. The text says the combined take is only a few points below FY2025, not a step change, and equals the nine-month run-rate. [S0][S9]

challenges.challenge: The cti basis in fund record still says the FY2026E total is '4.5pp below the 98.6% combined cost ratio the FY2025 P&L itself shows'. (Rp2,572.3bn + Rp220.0bn) / Rp2,939.8bn = 95.0%, so the gap is 3.6pp. A wrong arithmetic claim in a basis is the kind of figure the next auditor checks first, and it survives in the model file even if the report is corrected.
challenges.answer: Corrected to 3.6pp in the cti basis in fund record (98.6% less 95.0%). The same basis paragraph now also records that the 99.57% BOPO is a first-half gross-income ratio and is not used as a cap. No model value changed and the engine re-run is clean. [S0]

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says 'the base regime keeps 0.35 of the log gap, which is the premium-kept multiple applied to the twelve-month value, and gives a regime target of Rp84'. compress.base = 0.35 is the share of the log gap CLOSED (engine: fund record line 1490); the premium kept is 4.131x = exp(0.65 x 2.182), and 20.31 x 4.131 = Rp83.9 is what reproduces the target. As written the sentence implies a kept multiple near 1.4x and cannot reproduce Rp84.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now says the base regime closes 0.35 of the log gap, states explicitly that this is the share closed and not the share kept, and says the multiple applied to the twelve-month value is well above one - today's 8.9x spot premium raised to the unclosed share, which is 4.13x and equals Rp83.9 over Rp20.3. The premium-kept multiple is pointed to the konglo table for each regime, so the printed Rp84 reproduces. The bear and bull sentences now use the same closes/re-expands wording. [S0][S10]

challenges.challenge: Section 1 still opens 'Strategy as the board states it is capital repair and cost discipline' cited to [S5], but S5 (June 2026 AGM report) covers the FY2025 accounts, the profit allocation, the Recovery Plan update and the board change, and contains no cost or efficiency statement - and section 3 itself says 'It is not a savings programme and we cite none', so section 1 attributes to the board a strategy the report elsewhere disowns. Separately, section 6 says HSC status 'removes it from the main indices' cited to [S0], and neither S0 nor the company source set carries that fact; the konglo registry does (deck S3 for the list, S4 for the consequence).
challenges.answer: Section 1 now attributes only the AGM actions to S5 (accounts approved, statutory reserve, Rp28.97m retained, Recovery Plan updated, board changed) and drops 'cost discipline'; it now says we tested the filings for a cost programme and found none, so the cost line is anchored on the reported run-rate. Section 6 attributes HSC membership and the index consequence to the house konglo registry as of 27 October 2026, keeps 'not a finding of wrongdoing', and the same S0 mismatch is removed from sections 4 and 5. [S5][S0]

missing_bull_case.note: Licence/control value and LDR free capacity are absent. The thesis says the price is a control option, yet no M&A or licence precedent is cited and the bull run applies no CTI shock although its narrative claims 78% and 2.5% ROE. LDR 77.5% on Rp147trn of deposits is read only as an inability to originate, never as spare lending capacity.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear shocks only credit cost, NIM and growth. It omits the two largest tails: the Rp3trn injection failing (CAR 11.1% then forces shrinkage or a discounted rights issue, and shares are held flat while Rp5trn arrives), and a related-party/group or property-collateral event that the report itself says it cannot size.

assumption_realism.note: FY2026E non-interest income of Rp139bn is below the Rp250bn nine-month actual (S0), FY2026E earning assets fall 11% while total assets rise 7%, and the equity path ignores both the reported Rp19,079bn book (F12) and the Rp3,000bn still to be paid in (F16). The three largest value drivers are not mutually consistent.

evidence_and_citations.note: The rendered report states gross NPL 336.0%, net NPL 267.0% and NIM 252.0% because the pct filter multiplies percent-valued facts F5/F6/F8 by 100. Fact dates do not match their labels (F1 loans is per Juni 2025, F18 is 1H2025, F19 earning_assets is total assets), the 3.36% NPL has no supporting quote, and the 0.2%/0.4% credit charge and the 86.1% vs 24.5% ownership are unsourced.

valuation_method_fit.note: DDM is declared unavailable yet weighted 20% at zero, cutting the method blend from Rp42.5 to Rp34.0. Residual income adds a Rp19,079bn opening book but rolls forward on Rp17,173bn, so its Rp49 is an artefact. The decimal COE build uses ERP 6.69% against a 5.0-6.0% band, and the packet target line prints 40 x (1 - 20%) = 116 when that arithmetic gives 32.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose proves more than the numbers do: the summary says Rp32 is the fundamental value and that the stock trades at 5.7x it, but 161/32 is 5.0x and 5.7x requires the undisclosed spot value of Rp28.4. The mirror is exact only in the shocks, not in the narratives, and one sentence in 4 is ungrammatical and unverifiable.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The konglo deck parameters are applied (0.30/0.70/-0.15 plus hsc 0.05) but the free-float deadline adjustment is not, and the registry records the 24.5% float as compliant against a 15% minimum, which contradicts the report's 31 March 2027 forced-float catalyst. The VAL_BANKS output contract also lacks deposit beta, CASA/TD path, CET1 headroom and a three-year BVPS path.

conservatism_audit.note: Conservative side: NOII 44% below the nine-month actual, a 20% liquidity discount and a beta of 1.10 both charged for thin float, plus DDM at zero. Optimistic side: a 0.2%/0.4% credit charge with gross NPL rising from 3.26% (Jun-25) to 4.02% (Jun-26), no coverage ratio, and the Rp3trn injection treated as certain. Thick enough to move the rating in both directions.

calibration.note: The gate passes a 0.45pp ROE gap when FY2025A ROE is 0.176% and the model's FY+1 is 0.628%, three and a half times the last actual. The justification filed is calibration.unavailable, an orphan flag, so the real gap is unanswered; FY+1 also does not reproduce the run-rate (TOI Rp2,796bn against Rp2,973bn annualised).

signoff.notes: APPROVED, no challenges. House view is the most likely path: the FY2026E uplift to np +Rp110.6bn is the sourced 9M actual (IDR87.0bn) carried with a 0.2% provision charge that section 3 flags as borrowing from the future and normalises to 0.4% by FY2028E; sustainable ROE 0.24% against cost of equity 11.85% and g 0.0% (zero payout, ROE cap) gives 0.02x book, and the RI method floors at zero on limited liability - both stated. Scenarios are exactly mirrored (+/-0.3pp credit cost, 0.3pp NIM, 3pp loan growth) with base at 50%; konglo applies hsc 0.05 only and correctly does NOT apply the free-float deadline (registry 24.5% float, compliant), and the lens lifts Rp20 to Rp107 using the disclosed 8.9x spot premium - so it works against the SELL, which survives at -45% with the bull at 15%. The DDM exclusion is an argued departure (zero payout), not a zero weight, and the target Rp107 = 0.25x35 + 0.5x84 + 0.25x224. Four NOTEs are text-only and change no number; the Director should copy-edit: (1) Q16 use IDR29.0bn (not 30.0bn) in section 1, the AGM retained Rp28.97bn after the Rp1bn reserve; (2) Q17 rewrite the closing clause of params_basis - the 13.9% public-holding claim contradicts sections 4 and 6 and the registry (24.5% float, compliant); float is charged once, in the liquidity discount; (3) Q18 state in section 3 that CAR 11.09% [S2] is used and disclose that S10 gives 13-14%; (4) Q19 carry Q12/Q14 into the next update.

bias.note: Base is anchored on the last actuals, not on a view: FY2026E opex plus provisions of Rp2,792.3bn is 95.0% of TOI Rp2,939.8bn against the 9M2026 actual envelope of 95.1% (TOI Rp2,225.3bn less PBT Rp108.8bn, S0), NII and NOII sit on the 9M actual within 1%, and the 0.20%-to-0.40% credit path is disclosed and stressed at x3 in the bear. Scenarios are mirrored (+/-0.3pp credit cost, +/-0.3pp NIM, +/-3pp loan growth, base 50%, S0). The departures toward caution (NIM 1.55%-1.80% vs the 1H2025 2.52% on a 77%-earning-asset base, zero terminal growth, 20% liquidity discount) are each sourced or arithmetically driven, and the free-float adjustment the deck allows is NOT applied, so the lens is the generous side of the call. No unexplained optimism in the base; the SELL rests on a 0.2% sustainable ROE against an 11.9% COE, not on a stack of haircuts.

recomputed.item: Sep-2026 loans implied by LDR 77.45% on DPK 147,400 vs model FY2026E

findings.finding: Section 1 says the AGM retained the remaining IDR30.0bn; section 6 says IDR29.0bn and fact F25 (S5) records Rp28.97bn retained after the Rp1bn statutory reserve, so 30.0bn is the net profit, not the remainder.

params_basis still asserts the controller's 86.1% holding is 13.9% public and below the 15% minimum, while sections 4 and 6 say the public holding is not asserted to be below the minimum and the konglo registry records the 24.5% float field as compliant (hsc true, registry asof 27 Oct 2026). The lens is unaffected: the free-float-deadline adjustment is not applied on either reading.

Two archived sources disagree on September 2026 CAR: F7/S2 gives 11.09% (up from 10.09%) and S10 gives 13-14 percent in the same September-2026 sentence as the 2.67% net NPL. The report and the rwa_density basis use 11.09% without disclosing the conflict; it is the conservative of the two and supports the close-to-the-floor risk line.

The house judge this round also raises the unused probability-1.0 Rp3,000bn bridge line (already Q14) and the Q12 opening-book double count; both are disclosed in sections 3 and 4 and immaterial to the target.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'justified_pbv': 0.5, 'residual_income': 0.3, 'ddm': 0.2}
flags.justification: Residual income is the VAL_BANKS primary and carries 50% with warranted P/BV as the 50% cross-check; the dividend discount method is dropped, not weighted at zero, because the payout is zero by policy and has been in every year of the data history [S0][S5] and a zero-payout DDM returns zero for arithmetic reasons rather than for a view, so weighting it dilutes the value. The industry default keeps a 20% DDM weight, which is the only difference from this file.

flags.message: konglo lens: price is 8.87x fundamental value (premium); the base case closes 35% of the log gap in 12 months (hsc); target 107 vs fundamental 12-month value 20 — explain it in §4 and §6
flags.justification: The price is a float premium, not a fundamental price: the data pack records the controller and affiliates at 86.06% and a separate free-float field of 24.5% [S0], and those two fields cannot both be right, so the public holding is between the residual to the insider figure and the pack's float field. On either reading the marginal seller is scarce and the lens applies. The regime target keeps only the part of the log premium the deck says persists inside twelve months (base compression 0.35 plus the HSC adjustment of 0.05), and the free-float-deadline adjustment of +0.05 is not applied because the registry records the pack's float as compliant [S0]; applied, it would compress further and lower the target, so the lens as run is the generous side of the call. The gap between the lens target and the fundamental twelve-month value is the premium we judge most likely to persist, and the SELL rests on even that generous number sitting below the price.
